# Overview

This notebook documents the full development arc of the microbiome analysis project, including initial preprocessing attempts, roadblocks encountered, the decision to pivot, and the new profiling/analysis direction. It serves as a transparent record of reasoning, environment changes, and project structure evolution.

# 1. Project Background

## 1.1 Dataset

This project uses **curatedMetagenomicData**, a large, high‑quality collection of human microbiome datasets processed using MetaPhlAn3 (taxonomic profiling) and HUMAnN3 (functional profiling). All data is accessed directly in R, with no preprocessing or command‑line tools required.

## 1.2 Original Goals

The project originally aimed to build a full preprocessing pipeline (QC, trimming, host removal, environment setup). After encountering environment instability, the workflow pivoted toward a profiling‑first approach using curatedMetagenomicData.

## 1.3 Updated Pipeline Plan

The project now focuses on: - Loading MetaPhlAn3 + HUMAnN3 outputs directly from curatedMetagenomicData\
- Performing downstream ecological and functional analysis in R\
- Building multiple infant gut microbiome projects (cross‑sectional + disease-focused)

# 2. Preprocessing Phase Summary

## 2.1 What Was Attempted

Summaries of: - QC reports generated\
- Host removal setup\
- Environment configuration\
- Initial R scripts created

## 2.2 What Worked

- Folder structure was established.\
- QC reports were successfully generated.\
- Environment setup was partially documented.

## 2.3 What Didn’t Work

- Host removal pipeline stalled due to environment conflicts.\
- Some preprocessing steps became redundant after pivoting to profiling-first tools.\
- R scripts became outdated relative to the new direction.

## 2.4 Lessons Learned

- Preprocessing pipelines are heavy and brittle without stable environments.\
- Profiling-first workflows (MetaPhlAn, HUMAnN) reduce complexity.\
- Documentation must evolve with the project.

# 3. Pivot Decision

## 3.1 Why Pivot

The original pipeline required Ubuntu, WSL2, micromamba, and multiple command‑line tools. After environment failures and recognizing that curatedMetagenomicData provides clean, ready‑to‑analyze MetaPhlAn3/HUMAnN3 outputs, the project pivoted to a fully R‑based workflow.

## 3.2 New Pipeline Direction

- Use curatedMetagenomicData as the data source\
- Begin analysis directly from taxonomic and functional profiles\
- Focus on infant gut microbiome (Project B)\
- Expand to disease-focused infant cohorts (Project C)\
- Use Quarto notebooks for documentation and reproducibility
